id: title:Gilbert09:add 3 missing tables to the youtube analytics source

review.posthog_relevance: Adds warehouse ingestion support for YouTube Analytics reports (Traffic Source Details, Audience Retention, Videos) with full-refresh-only handling, while backend helper functions for metadata and retention retrieval are also supplied.
review.reason: The chunk includes substantive warehouse ingestion implementation and backend helper functions. P1.F6.H3 and P1.F5.H4 demonstrate the addition of new report types with full-refresh-only status and relevant assertions, while P1.F7.H7 supplies backend helper functions for retrieving video and audience retention data. This represents a bounded capability improvement for warehouse data
review.uncertainty: No tests, migrations, or frontend changes are supplied; warehouse-side implementation and complete orchestration context are not available, and the chunk is dominated by backend and warehouse ingestion, with no complete context of warehouse ingestion, scheduling or failure handling.

observations.behavior: Adds a new report type, TRAFFIC_SOURCE_DETAILS, with its own dimensions and primary key, and its own full-refresh-only status.
observations.posthog_connection: Warehouse ingestion for YouTube Analytics now supports a new report, traffic source details, while retaining the existing incremental-only reports. This report lacks a day grain, so it cannot support incremental syncs; the warehouse ingestion must treat it as a full-refresh-only report. This could help PostHog users obtain traffic source breakdowns without risking incremental syncs

observations.behavior: Adds a new report type, AUDIENCE_RETENTION, with its own dimensions and primary key, and its own full-refresh-only status.
observations.posthog_connection: Warehouse ingestion for YouTube Analytics now supports audience retention, a report that lacks a day grain. This report cannot support incremental syncs; the warehouse ingestion must treat it as a full-refresh-only report. This could help PostHog users obtain audience retention without risking incremental syncs
